title: Volume of Cylinders, Cones and Spheres
seo_title: Volume of Solids – JSS 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the volume and surface area of cylinders, cones and spheres; solve problems with solids. (summary of the NERDC JSS 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 maths worksheets on mensuration of solids: volume of cylinders, cones and spheres, answers in terms of π, and problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume of a cylinder = πr²h.
  • Volume of a cone = ⅓πr²h. It is one third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
  • Volume of a sphere = ⁴⁄₃πr³.

Examples

Example

Cone with r = 3 cm, h = 7 cm (π = 22/7)

⅓ × 22/7 × 9 × 7

Answer: 66 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the ⅓ for a coneA cone is one third of a cylinder.
Using the diameterHalve it to get the radius.
Cubing the radius for a cylinderCylinder uses r², sphere uses r³.

faq.a: The cylinder, three times as much.
